messages.content:
Add to this Python module a function `tag_path(tag)`: the path of a tag's page, `/tags/` followed by the tag as it goes in a URL, like `/tags/live-music`.

```python
"""Paths of the blog's pages."""
import re
import unicodedata


def slugify(title):
    """The URL form of a title: no accents, lower case, words joined by '-' ('Cafe con Leche!' -> 'cafe-con-leche')."""
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text.lower()).strip("-")


def article_path(year, title):
    """The path of an article: '/2026/cafe-con-leche'."""
    return f"/{year}/{slugify(title)}"
```

The module already turns a name into its URL form: `slugify` drops the accents, lowers the case and joins the words with `-`, and `article_path` uses it. `tag_path` calls it too. A second conversion written for tags (`tag.lower().replace(" ", "-")`) would keep the accents and the punctuation that the article paths drop, and the two kinds of path would disagree on the first tag with an accent.

```python
"""Paths of the blog's pages."""
import re
import unicodedata


def slugify(title):
    """The URL form of a title: no accents, lower case, words joined by '-' ('Cafe con Leche!' -> 'cafe-con-leche')."""
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text.lower()).strip("-")


def article_path(year, title):
    """The path of an article: '/2026/cafe-con-leche'."""
    return f"/{year}/{slugify(title)}"


def tag_path(tag):
    """The path of a tag's page: '/tags/live-music'."""
    return f"/tags/{slugify(tag)}"
```

meta.teaches: look at what the module already has before writing; the URL form of a name is the slug function it has, not a second one
